item.title: NBR cuts import duties on dates, apples, and oranges ahead of Ramadan
item.description:
The National Board of Revenue (NBR) has reduced import duties on dates, apples, and oranges to keep their prices under control during the upcoming holy month of Ramadan.
According to a gazette notification issued on Tuesday, the import duty on dates has been slashed from 25% to 5%, bringing the total tax incidence on date imports down from 48% to 25%.
This reduced rate will remain in effect until March 10, 2027.
For apples and oranges, the regulatory duty has been reduced to 5%, while supplementary duty and VAT have been set at 20%.
Following these adjustments, the total tax incidence on apples and oranges will drop sharply from 121% to 48%.
The notification stated that the revised rates for apples and oranges will be effective from January 24 to February 23, 2027.
The NBR expects that the duty cuts will boost imports and ensure an adequate supply of these fruits, helping to stabilize market prices.
The decision to lower duties on these import-dependent fruits was reportedly taken a few days ago during a cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
Currently, different varieties of dates are selling between Tk200 and Tk2,000 per kilogram in Dhaka’s kitchen markets, while apples are priced at Tk300–500 per kg and oranges at Tk400–600 per kg.

item.title: Mahila Parishad concerned over rising violence against women, children in Brahmanbaria
item.description:
Bangladesh Mahila Parishad’s Brahmanbaria district committee has expressed concern over a series of incidents of rape, sexual abuse, torture and murder involving women and children in the district.
The concern was raised at a press conference held at Brahmanbaria Press Club Wednesday afternoon, marking the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women 2026.
Nelly Akter, vice-president of the district committee, chaired the event, while its general secretary, Shyama Sikder Dina, presented the written statement.
In her statement, Dina said poverty, social inequality and a lack of family and social awareness were among the factors contributing to violence against women and children.
She called for collective efforts to prevent such incidents, ensure justice and protection for survivors, and end the culture of impunity.
She identified Brahmanbaria Sadar, Akhaura and Nabinagar upazilas as areas with comparatively high numbers of reported incidents of violence against women and children.
Poverty, lack of family awareness, complexities within joint families, extramarital relationships and arrogance among some middle- and upper-income families were also cited as contributing factors.
According to the organisation, several incidents of violence against women and children were reported in the district between January and November 2026.
On April 11, a housewife was beaten to death in Nabinagar. On April 28, a teenage girl was reportedly raped in the Baganbari area of Ashuganj upazila.
On April 30, a doctor couple was arrested over allegations of torturing a 12-year-old domestic worker in North Mourail area of Brahmanbaria municipality.
In another incident, seven-year-old Mahida Akter was allegedly raped and strangled to death on September 25 in Andidil village under Talshahar Union of Ashuganj upazila.
A post-mortem report published on September 26 reportedly found evidence of rape and identified excessive bleeding and strangulation as the causes of death. The accused, Zahidul Islam, was arrested in connection with the case.
The organisation also cited the alleged rape of a five-year-old child with disabilities in Nasirnagar upazila and the rape of a madrasa student on October 7.
As part of the 16-day campaign marking the occasion, the district committee will conduct awareness programmes across the district from November 25 to December 10.
The programmes will include discussions with young people, women and men, meetings with administrative officials and lawyers, leaflet distribution, poster-drawing activities and other awareness initiatives.
Among those present were district committee vice-president Geeta Roy, publicity secretary Kohinoor Akter Priya, training secretary Masuma Khanam, movement secretary Ratna Das and committee member Laboni Rani Das.
Journalists from various print and electronic media outlets attended the press conference.

item.title: Batighar: A beacon of knowledge in remote villages of Tangail
item.description:
What began with around 100 books in a small room of his family home has grown into a community reading initiative with more than 2,000 books, 219 registered members and several thousand occasional readers.
Mohammad Kamruzzaman, a resident of Chourakorra village in Tangail's Magra Union, established the library, named Batighar, on February 21, 2010, while he was a university student.
Beyond its main library, the initiative has expanded to bus counters, railway stations and local salons, creating opportunities for people to read while waiting for buses, trains or haircuts.
Initially, Kamruzzaman used books from his personal collection and contributions from friends to set up the library in a room of his family home. Over the years, it has developed into a community resource where people of all ages can read books, borrow them and access information.
Readers can become members by following the library's rules. Books can be borrowed for 15 days, and those unable to visit the library can request delivery over the phone.
Kamruzzaman moved to Tangail town after completing his secondary education. He later enrolled at Mawlana Bhashani Science and Technology University, where he studied in the Department of Criminology and Police Science. After graduation, he joined Bangladesh Police as a sub-inspector. He is currently serving at the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI).
Seeking to make reading accessible beyond the library's premises, Kamruzzaman introduced mini libraries at different public places.
At Tangail's new bus terminal, several bus-counter mini libraries allow passengers to read while waiting for their buses.
He also launched a free reading programme at local salons, calling it the "Salon Mini Library". A total of 10 such libraries have been established at salons in Kuijbari, Ayanapur, Chourakorra, Nandabala and Magra Bazar in Tangail Sadar Upazila, as well as Palima Bazar in Kalihati Upazila.
A similar facility has been introduced at Tangail Railway Station, where a wooden bookshelf has been installed on the main platform. Passengers can choose books, read while waiting for their trains and return them afterwards.
Rakib Hossain, a passenger waiting for the Dhaka-bound Silk City Express, welcomed the initiative.
"This is a very commendable initiative. We often have to wait at the station for trains. The environment here is pleasant for reading. Now we can spend our waiting time reading books and enjoying ourselves," he said.
Several college students from the village help manage the library's activities.
Seema Akter, one of the student volunteers, said the library remains open from the afternoon until evening every day except Thursday.
"Books are regularly borrowed and returned during this time. Each book can be borrowed for 15 days. If someone has difficulty visiting the library, they can call us, and we arrange to deliver the book to them," she said.
Sumaiya Akter, a Class Ten student at Magra High School for Girls, said the library had made reading more accessible for students.
"Having this library has been very helpful for us. We can borrow books whenever we want," she said.
Local businessman Chhanowar Hossain, who enjoys reading during his leisure time, is also a regular member of the library.
Mahbub Hasan, a National University student and regular reader, said residents previously had to travel several kilometres to reach the district public library.
"Travelling there was difficult and time-consuming. Even when we wanted to read, we could not always manage to go. With this library, we now have much easier access to books," he said.
However, he said the collection and the library's furniture and other facilities needed further improvement.
Anisur Rahman, acting headteacher of Choudhury Malanch High School, said the library was helping develop reading habits among local residents.
"Alongside their textbooks, students are reading different kinds of books and enriching their knowledge. I believe this will help illuminate their future," he said, calling on education enthusiasts and financially capable members of society to support the library's development.
Kamruzzaman has received several awards for his contribution to promoting reading habits and establishing libraries in rural communities.
His recognitions include the Prothom Alo Bondhushava Award 2021, Pathshala Emerging Leader Award 2022, Institution Library Award 2023, Alor Ferry Library Digitisation Award and the Bangladesh Bookworm Association Special Recognition Award 2024.
Batighar's readers have also achieved recognition. Recently, library member Fawzia Haque Jinat was selected as the country's best participant at the school level in a national book-reading competition organised by the National Book Centre.
Kamruzzaman's father, Shahjahan, said he was initially doubtful about the initiative.
"When Kamruzzaman first established the library, I thought he was doing something unusual. But after a few days, I realised it was a very good initiative. That is why I allowed him to use a room in our house," he said.
Kamruzzaman said the initiative was intended to help people who love reading but cannot afford to buy books regularly.
To ensure the library's sustainability, he has formed a seven-member committee comprising local residents from different walks of life. The committee oversees its activities.
He is also trying to secure a permanent plot of land in the village to build a dedicated library.
"We are gradually moving forward with everyone's support. I hope that one day we will be able to establish our own building with a rich collection of books and publications from home and abroad," he said.
He added that the initiative also aims to encourage teenagers and young people to develop reading habits, reduce excessive dependence on technology and engage in social and humanitarian activities.
"We want to spread these activities across the district and, eventually, throughout the country," he said.
For Kamruzzaman, Batighar is more than a library. It is an effort to make books accessible to people who might otherwise have limited opportunities to read.

item.title: Home minister: Police involved in political conspiracies to face action
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has warned that police officers involved in political conspiracies or activities violating their professional duties will face legal and departmental action, stressing that law enforcement personnel must remain politically impartial.
“Any involvement in political conspiracies or activities contrary to their official duties would invite legal and departmental action,” he said at a press briefing at the Home Ministry at the secretariat on Wednesday.
The minister said several police officers had already been arrested over allegations of political bias and conspiratorial activities while serving in Gopalganj. They are facing sedition charges alongside departmental proceedings, he added.
An additional superintendent of police, a resident of Muksudpur Upazila who was serving in the area, had also been withdrawn from duty, Salahuddin said.
On the ongoing labour unrest in the garment sector, the minister said the minimum wage had been finalised through the Minimum Wage Board with the consent of representatives of both employers and workers.
He claimed that genuine workers and factory owners were satisfied with the agreed wage structure, while certain groups were spreading rumours to fuel unrest in industrial areas.
Alleging that an unidentified group was trying to exploit the situation for political purposes, he said law enforcement agencies were investigating those allegedly instigating the unrest from behind the scenes.
He reiterated that the government would take necessary legal measures to maintain law and order and prevent disruptions in the industrial sector.

item.title: Dhaka urges South Africa to open resident mission
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Wednesday urged South Africa to consider opening a resident mission in Dhaka to strengthen political engagement, expand bilateral trade and streamline consular services.
He made the request when South Africa's non-resident High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Professor Anil Sooklal, paid a courtesy call on him at the foreign ministry here, according to a ministry press release.
Reaffirming Bangladesh's commitment to closer ties with South Africa, Kobir also called for simpler visa procedures for Bangladeshi businesspeople, officials, students and other travellers to the country.
Both sides noted the untapped potential for bilateral trade and investment.
Kobir called for establishing a Joint Trade Forum and exchanging high-level business delegations to boost trade.
The state minister thanked South Africa for its continued support for the Rohingya and urged it to remain engaged in international efforts to ensure their safe, voluntary, dignified and sustainable return to Myanmar.

item.title: Christian Aid launches Asia model to strengthen local leadership
item.description:
International development and humanitarian organisation Christian Aid has launched a new Asia Multi-Country Cluster (MCC) model aimed at shifting more decision-making powers and resources to local organisations and communities affected by crises.
The model was launched at an event in Gulshan-2, Dhaka, on Tuesday. It seeks to promote locally led development by giving local partners greater control over development and humanitarian initiatives.
Christian Aid Chief Executive Officer Patrick Watt introduced the new operating structure, describing it as a shift away from traditional top-down management towards an approach that positions the organisation as a connector and convener of local partners.
State Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shaikh Faridul Islam attended the event as chief guest, while NGO Affairs Bureau Director General (Secretary) Dr Mohammed Jakaria was present as special guest.
The event also highlighted Christian Aid's performance in the Grand Bargain Independent Report 2023–2026. According to the report, the organisation ranked first among global signatories in 2025, directing 82% of its humanitarian funding to local and national actors, against the Grand Bargain's target of 25%.
Christian Aid also outlined its Survivor and Community-Led Response (SCLR) approach, under which local self-help groups design and manage their own recovery projects rather than simply being consulted.
The organisation also highlighted its efforts to promote fair indirect cost recovery (ICR) for local partners, speed up emergency fund disbursement during disasters and simplify due diligence procedures.
Representatives of Bangladeshi partner organisations, including Bazle Mustafa Razee of FIVDB, Juliate Keya Malakar of CCDB and Sunzida Sultana of Karmojibi Nari, shared their experiences of working with Christian Aid.
Senior members of the Asia MCC team, including Head of Impact Douwe Dijkstra, Partnership and Strategy Lead Nuzhat Jabin, Operations Lead Azahar Ali and Bangladesh Programme and Partnership Lead Prince Baroi, discussed how the new structure would promote regional collaboration, cross-country learning and local leadership.

item.title: Sinner at risk of missing Australian Open after confirming knee surgery
item.description:
Jannik Sinner risks missing the Australian Open after confirming on Tuesday that he has undergone surgery on his troublesome right knee.
The five-time Grand Slam champion has not played a match since winning Wimbledon for the second time in July, with less than two months until the start of the first major tournament of the season in Melbourne.
"Over the past few months, together with my team we've tried everything to treat my injury without surgery," Sinner said in a statement.
"After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn't respond as we had all hoped, that's why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band."
The procedure, which had been reported earlier in the day by broadcasters RAI and Sky Sport, and sports daily La Gazzetta dello Sport, was performed by knee injury specialist Lasse Lempainen at a clinic in Finland.
Another knee specialist, Fabrizio Terrone at the Isokinetic centre in Turin, told Sky Sport that Sinner's absence could last "at least three to four months".
That means the earliest Sinner might be back on court with a racket in hand would be during the American hard-court swing, at Indian Wells and Miami Masters.
- Difficult times -
The 25-year-old admitted recently that the worst injury of his career left him barely able to move.
"The worst part for me about this injury is that I cannot compete, I cannot play tennis," said Sinner in a recent video.
"Also my life outside of tennis is a bit more limited because of a simple fact that I cannot do things that I really like, because I want to protect my knee."
Sinner, a two-time champion at the Australian Open which begins on January 17, recently said that he will make his comeback at the "Six Kings Slam" tournament in Saudi Arabia, which has been rescheduled for late December due to the conflict with Yemen's Houthis.
But that now looks impossible and a difficult start to 2027 seems in store for the man who has in recent years risen to be, alongside Spanish star Carlos Alcaraz, the pre-eminent force in men's tennis.
Sinner was having a brilliant campaign before being stopped by his knee problem, with five Masters 1000 titles going alongside his triumph at Wimbledon.
The Italian's 94 percent winning record in 2026 is the best of his career, even beating his figures from the previous two seasons in each of which he won two Grand Slams and the ATP Finals.
He suffered a major disappointment at the French Open when, leading Argentina's Juan Manuel Cerundolo by two sets and 5-1 ahead in the third, he succumbed to heat stroke and was eliminated in the second round.
Sinner recently lost top spot in the men's world rankings to losing Wimbledon finalist Alexander Zverev, who has taken advantage of injury problems for both Sinner and Alcaraz to win Roland Garros and the US Open.

item.title: 'Quite good at slogging' - England revel in new batting talent Donald
item.description:
Dynamic new England opener Aneurin Donald says he is not great at batting but "quite at slogging" after his blistering 85 against Australia thrust him into the global Twenty20 spotlight.
England's all-Welsh opening partnership of Donald and Phil Salt produced a brutal display of power hitting at the Gold Coast on Tuesday as the visitors won the second of their five-match series by eight wickets.
They shared in a 151-run stand with Aneurin slamming nine sixes and four boundaries in his stunning knock off just 32 balls.
His maiden 50 came from 18 deliveries -- the joint third-fastest for England in the format with the innings propelling Donald's T20 strike rate since the beginning of 2024 to 216.37.
That moved him ahead of Indian teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (212.84) as the world's fastest scorer across the past three years, according to Cricket Australia statistics.
"I've realised I'm not great at batting, but quite good at slogging," said Donald on the change of technique that has seen him break into the England team.
"Releasing that pressure on myself, and I treat every bowler, whoever it is, on whatever stage, at whatever ground or whatever conditions, trying to stay true to myself.
"It's obviously easier said than done when I put a few up the chute early, but it's just trusting my bat swing, and I feel like I've been in a pretty good place in my game for a little while now."
Former England captain Michael Vaughan told the BBC it was a night where "we saw a player really step up to the big stage" with his exploits likely to attract interest from Indian Premier League franchises.
"He's got a few franchise gigs at the moment but to do it on the biggest stage against Australia, with the world watching, he's going to be talked about," added Vaughan.
Donald produced four low scores to start his international career, and credited coach Brendon McCullum telling him to "just be free" for his turnaround on the Gold Coast.
"It's been a mad few months and hopefully I can keep riding the wave," said the 29-year-old, who will stay in Australia after the series for the Big Bash League.
He will open the batting for the Perth Scorchers alongside Australia white-ball captain Mitchell Marsh, who could only watch in awe.
"I'm looking forward to suiting up with Mitch. He kept walking past me, saying, 'Well batted, partner', which was a nice feeling," said Donald.

item.title: Sooryavanshi smashes 204 off 53 balls to rewrite record books
item.description:
India's teenage opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi rewrote the List A record books on Tuesday, hitting 204 off 53 balls with 28 sixes for India A against the United Arab Emirates at the Asia Cup Rising Stars tournament in Doha.
His 28 sixes are the most by a batsman in an innings in any form of senior recognised cricket.
Sooryavanshi reached his century off 28 balls, his 150 off 40 and his double century off 52, all List A records.
The previous record for the fastest List A hundred belonged to Australia's Jake Fraser-McGurk, who reached three figures off 29 balls for South Australia in the Marsh Cup in 2023.
Sooryavanshi already held the record for the fastest List A 150, set off 59 balls in the Vijay Hazare Trophy last year, and broke it again by 19 balls.
New Zealand's Chad Bowes had held the record for the fastest List A double century, reaching 200 off 103 balls. Sooryavanshi got there in almost half that time.
He reached his first fifty on Tuesday off 16 balls. He also holds the record for the fastest List A fifty, made off 11 balls earlier this year.
His strike rate of 384.90 is also the highest for a List A innings of this length.
The previous record for most sixes in an innings in recognised cricket was 26, by Tanmay Agarwal during his 366 in a four-day Ranji Trophy match. The List A record was 23, shared by Darcy Short and Colin Munro.
Sooryavanshi’s innings took India A to a 250-run target in 14.2 overs, the fastest successful chase of more than 200 in List A cricket.

item.title: Arteta backs 'brilliant' Gyokeres after Arsenal waste chances to beat Dortmund
item.description:
Mikel Arteta defended Viktor Gyokeres after the inconsistent Arsenal striker's "unbelievable" strike was followed by a costly miss in Tuesday's 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League.
Arteta had urged Gyokeres to seize his opportunity after selecting the Sweden striker instead of Kai Havertz for the league phase tie at the Emirates Stadium.
Initially, Gyokeres looked like doing just that with his first goal at home this season, and only his third for the Gunners in all competitions.
But the 28-year-old has been much-maligned for his erratic displays since arriving from Sporting Lisbon in 2025.
And he gave more ammunition to his critics when he missed a golden opportunity to seal the points with a woeful header in the closing stages.
Leaping to Gyokeres's defence, Arteta said: "He had a brilliant performance today. He scored an unbelievable goal. He has the quality to do that.
"What I loved the most was how connected he was to the team. We used him many times in different ways, his link-up play, the way he held the ball.
"He got behind and stretched the pitch. There was a lot to like in that performance."
Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 11 games in all competitions, but this was not a vintage display by the English champions, who failed to win at home for the first time this season.
Arteta disagreed, insisting Arsenal were deserving of all three points on the balance of play.
"The way we played, there is no question how superior, how dominant, how much of a threat we were. It was great to watch. It was unbelievable that sometimes the ball didn't go in the back of the net," he said.
"The execution can be better, we rushed a little bit. Certainly we could have finished the actions better today.
"There is an element of luck, how the hell some of those balls didn't go in, I don't know. There is an element of us needing to finish the actions better."
- 'Courageous' -
Arsenal sit fifth in the league phase with three wins and two draws from their five matches, while seventh-placed Dortmund are one point behind them.
Arteta will hope for a much more ruthless display in a significant Premier League showdown with spluttering title rivals Manchester City in north London on Sunday.
"What the team has shown today is a step in the right direction. There is a lot to like but obviously we want to win every game," he said.
Dortmund had equalised through Maximilian Beier prior to Gyokeres's key miss.
The Bundesliga leaders were well worth a point for their gritty display and boss Niko Kovac said: "This is a big one for all of us, the players, the fans and the club -- a big point away to Arsenal.
"In the first 15 minutes we didn't play the way I hoped. We were too passive.
"We were more courageous and pressed more actively after the break. We got Arsenal into difficult situations.
"We came back because of our huge desire. I'm really happy for the boys."

item.title: Mourinho hails 'extraordinary' Bellingham after wondergoal
item.description:
Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho hailed Jude Bellingham's game-changing display in the 5-1 Champions League rout of PSV on Tuesday.
The England international came on at half-time with Los Blancos trailing and inspired a sensational second half display, including scoring a magnificent effort from distance.
Bellingham had given Mourinho credit for helping him find arguably the best form he has enjoyed at Madrid in recent weeks, with Los Blancos winning a 10th straight match, but the coach said the midfielder only had himself to thank.
"I think the main figure responsible for what Jude is today is Jude, and his team-mates. I try to help a little," said the Portuguese coach.
"He's an absolutely extraordinary player who has everything -- he has physicality, he has technique, he has tactical understanding of the game, he has ambition, he has absolutely everything and today, obviously not by himself, but he changed the direction of the match.
"He's an absolutely extraordinary player and for me, without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world."
Madrid's victory over the Dutch champions maintained their 100 percent start to the league phase, in which they are provisional leaders.
Mourinho reiterated his view that it was a "scandal" that Bellingham was not ranked in the top 10 players in the world at this year's Ballon d'Or ceremony.
The coach said his team's performance in the first half was dreadful, trailing PSV 1-0 at half-time, and that Bellingham was key in turning it around.
"The first half was shocking," added Mourinho. "This number five gave the team a totally different dynamic."
Bellingham said he "did not know" how he scored his brilliant goal, flicking the ball up on the edge of the box and slicing a stunning effort inside the far post.
The English midfielder, upon joining Real Madrid, took Zinedine Zidane's number five shirt in "homage" to the Frenchman, whom he admired, and some have compared his goal against PSV to a Zidane-style strike.
"I do things that you guys think are similar to Zidane, but he was much better than me," Bellingham told reporters.

item.title: Bellingham beauty in Real win as Arsenal, City held in Champions League
item.description:
Jude Bellingham scored one of the goals of the season as Real Madrid hammered PSV Eindhoven 5-1 on Tuesday to maintain their perfect record in this season's Champions League, while Arsenal and Manchester City were both held to draws at home.
Elsewhere, debutants Como and Real Betis continued their excellent form since the start of the league phase, but Aston Villa slumped to another defeat on their travels.
Record 15-time European champions Real had to come from behind to beat PSV at the Bernabeu as they made it five wins from five in this season's league phase to go clear at the top of the standings with 15 points.
Dutch champions PSV led at half-time courtesy of an Ivan Perisic penalty, but Federico Valverde equalised five minutes after the restart.
Bellingham then put Real ahead on the hour with a remarkable strike, as he controlled a Kylian Mbappe lay-off outside the box and then teed himself up for a sweet volley on the outside of his right boot which flew into the corner of the net.
Mbappe then scored twice to move to 19 goals in all competitions this season and 76 career Champions League goals. The France captain now has 105 Real Madrid goals, one more than the Brazilian Ronaldo managed for the club.
Vinicius Junior sealed the win for Jose Mourinho's side, who have now claimed 10 consecutive victories in all competitions.
"That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and then I just hit it. I thought I would go with the outside of the boot a little bit, stab it a little bit, I am not one for smashing the ball too hard. It was a nice moment," England star Bellingham told British broadcaster TNT Sports about his goal.
Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain can join Real at the top of the standings if they beat Roma on Wednesday, but Como and Betis are currently level with the French side on 12 points after they beat AEK Athens and Slovan Bratislava respectively.
- Como and Betis flying -
Luis Milla scored as Como beat AEK 1-0 in Italy after Lucas Da Cunha earlier squandered a penalty, while Cucho Hernandez grabbed both goals for Betis in their 2-0 victory in Slovakia.
Arsenal had to settle for a point after drawing 1-1 with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium, as Viktor Gyokeres put the Gunners ahead but later missed a golden chance to win the game.
Gyokeres opened the scoring with a thunderous strike, but Maximilian Beier equalised for Dortmund and the Arsenal striker headed woefully wide from Martin Odegaard's cross late on.
It is the second time Arsenal, last season's beaten finalists, have dropped points to German opposition this season following a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich.
Manchester City are in the midst of a poor run of form in the Premier League and Enzo Maresca's side had to come from behind twice in the second half to draw 2-2 against Napoli.
Rasmus Hojlund, formerly of Manchester United, gave the Italians the lead early in the second half only for Ayyoub Bouaddi to equalise.
Kevin De Bruyne was returning to face his former side and he saw his Napoli team retake the lead through Noa Lang in the 76th minute, but Rayan Cherki's fine late goal earned City a point.
City won 10 of their first 11 games this season under Maresca. But the wheels have come off in the wake of the club being found guilty of widespread breaches of Premier League financial rules.
- Aston Villa lose -
"We don't like these moments - we want to win games - but unfortunately this moment is like this," said Maresca, ahead of a trip to Premier League champions Arsenal on Sunday.
None of the Premier League's representatives in the competition won on Tuesday, with Villa losing 1-0 to Galatasaray in Istanbul as Deniz Gul scored the only goal of the game late on. The two clubs are now level on nine points in the standings.
Portuguese champions Porto won 1-0 at Feyenoord thanks to Oussama Targhalline's early own-goal, while Antonio Nusa netted twice as RB Leipzig beat Lens 3-1 -- that was a fourth straight Champions League loss for the French team.
A stoppage-time own-goal gave Bodo/Glimt a 1-0 victory against Austria's LASK in Norway.

item.title: The epidemic we continue to tolerate
item.description:
Every year, November 25 is observed as the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Violence against women appears in a myriad of forms, ranging from wife abuse to rape, dowry killings, acid throwing, sexual harassment, and sexual slavery through international trafficking in women .
Violence against women has many causes, including patriarchal domination, forced marriage, gender stereotypes, lack of gender sensitivity, corruption in the judicial system, unequal power relations, unemployment, feminization of poverty, or trafficking of women.
In addition, low levels of education, low socio-economic status, younger age, alcohol abuse, childhood experience of abuse, witnessing violence between parents, lack of communication between partners, and living in communities with stronger norms of masculine dominance are among some of the determinants.
In different cultures around the world, socio-cultural norms deepen the subjugation of women. Societies press women to ensure abuse to protect family honour and the acceptance of male dominance. It contributes to normalization of domestic violence.
Violence against women is a global phenomenon that cuts across boundaries of age, socioeconomic status, education, and geography. Estimates by the World Health Organization (WHO) indicate that about 35% of women and girls worldwide have experienced physical and, or sexual intimate partner violence or non-partner sexual violence in their lifetime.
However, these numbers only tell a part of the story. Even when data is available, it is likely that the figures are an underestimate as it is notoriously difficult to collect sensitive information on violence against women, when the victims can fear coming forward or feel ashamed.
The impact of domestic violence is catastrophic, impairing the physical and psychological health of survivors, as well as their social and economic stability. Children who are witnesses to domestic violence are more likely to experience poor developmental outcomes and boys growing up in abusive households are likely to repeat the behaviours of their fathers in their own households when they grow up.
Even though various studies suggest that women in poor households are at a higher risk of domestic violence, the link between poverty and violence is poorly understood.
Violence against women also has an impact on the lives of many women beyond the direct victims. The fear of violence can prevent women from pursuing education, working, or exercising their political rights and voice.
In every region of the world, women consistently feel more insecure than men, although the levels of insecurity significantly vary across regions. Violence against women is not only a cause of gender inequality, it is also a consequence of it.
In many places, gender-based violence is reinforced by discriminatory laws and exclusionary social norms that undermine women and girls' opportunities for education, income, and independence. This accompanies shifting power relations within households and communities, especially when there is resentment against women who move away from conventional roles.
Detailed data from BBS suggests that adolescent girls, regardless of their marital status, continue to be vulnerable to all forms of violence. The hidden battle faced by victims of domestic violence is within the household -- they are isolated, without support or resources, suffering in silence, fearing further abuse or retribution, and are subject to shame and stigma which further inhibit them from seeking assistance or reporting abuses.
Globally, combating domestic violence requires a comprehensive strategy. It is essential to enhance legal protections for victims and ensure accountability for perpetrators. For all these, domestic violence laws must be enacted and enforced.
These will also involve improving police and judicial responsiveness, and guaranteeing violence victims access to legal aid and protection orders for survivors. Specific approaches and measures are needed for combatting increased domestic violence during shocks and vulnerabilities as seen during the Covid-19 pandemic.
In order to break the cycle of abuse, it is essential to transform societal views on domestic violence. This can be done through public awareness campaigns, educational initiatives, and community programs. It is necessary to challenge the norms and beliefs that sustain domestic violence, fostering a culture where violence is unacceptable and survivors are supported and empowered.
Policy interventions should focus on the longer-term by changing discriminatory social norms, closing gender gaps or building awareness. Innovative and aggressive policy that aims to change outcomes (such as increasing women’s voice in the community) may change norms. Although norms should guide the design of culturally sensitive policies and programs, they should not constrain or undermine initiatives.
Enhancing support services for domestic violence survivors is critical. This involves creating safe shelters, offering counselling and healthcare, and providing economic empowerment programs to help survivors rebuild their lives.
Ensuring these services are accessible and meet the diverse needs of all survivors, regardless of their socio-economic background or location, is vital. And so much more effort is needed to tackle the patterns of violence that cut deep into many societies so that they are not perpetuated across generations.
Several factors hinder victims from seeking help such as
Violence against women requires immediate and ongoing action. It demands a collective effort from the government, civil society, communities, and individuals to challenge the cultural and social norms enabling domestic violence, protect and support survivors, and hold perpetrators accountable.
Dr Selim Jahan is Former Director, Human Development Report Office and Poverty Division, United Nations Development Program, New York, USA.

item.title: Understanding the rise of divorce
item.description:
On a humid Tuesday morning, Rumana, 29, sits on a plastic chair outside a zonal office of the Dhaka South City Corporation, a brown envelope on her lap. Inside it is a notice that will end her seven-year marriage. She is a schoolteacher. Her husband stopped speaking to her months ago, except to remind her that his mother wanted a grandson and a larger share of her salary. Her parents once told her to be patient. This time, her father came with her.
Rumana is a composite, drawn from accounts reported in Bangladeshi newspapers, but her queue is real. In 2022, the two city corporations of Dhaka received 13,288 divorce applications, about 37 a day, or one every 40 minutes. Seven in 10 were filed by wives. Behind each envelope is a story Bangladesh has long preferred not to tell.
Bangladesh's crude divorce rate doubled in a single year, from 0.7 per 1,000 people in 2021 to 1.4 in 2022, according to the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS). For 15 years before that, between 2006 and 2021, it had moved only between 0.6 and 1.1. The rate eased to 1.1 in 2023, but it is still well above where it stood before the pandemic.
The numbers also break a familiar assumption. Divorce is often treated as an urban, middle-class phenomenon, yet BBS found it is higher in villages: 1.1 per 1,000 in rural areas in 2023, against 0.9 in cities. Division by division, the gap is wide: Rajshahi recorded 2.2 per 1,000, while Dhaka division stood at 1.3.
In the capital, the city corporations count every notice. Dhaka North alone received 5,459 applications in 2024, and 5,305 of them became effective divorces. Reconciliation, which the law requires the authorities to attempt within 90 days, almost never works: In Dhaka North in 2022, only 128 couples, about 2%, settled their differences.
The most striking change is who signs the notice. In Dhaka, about 70% of divorce applications are filed by women; in Dhaka North, women filed 4,081 of 7,414 notices in 2021, and employed women topped the list. City officials describe a quiet shift at home as well: Parents who once sent daughters back to abusive in-laws now increasingly help them file to protect them.
The shift is not only urban. In a village in Rajshahi, the division with the country's highest divorce rate, a 23-year-old woman, married at 16 to a man who left for Saudi Arabia within a year, waits each month for remittances that stop coming and phone calls that grow shorter.
When she finally hears that he has married again abroad, she sends her divorce notice through the local kazi . Her story, too, is a composite, but it echoes a pattern officials describe across the north: Young brides, long absences, and marriages that exist mostly on paper.
The reasons people give are older than the trend. BBS's 2022 survey, which for the first time asked divorced people directly, found extramarital relationships to be the leading cause. Alongside it sit dowry demands, physical and mental abuse, interference from in-laws, and long separations as husbands migrate abroad for work.
More women now earn their own money, more have finished school, and a smartphone can connect a woman in a village to a lawyer, a hotline or a friend who left before her.
Early marriage makes many of these unions fragile from the start. BBS found that 40.9% of those who married in 2022 were under 18, and 6.5% were under 15. The average age at marriage was 18.8 years for women and 25.3 for men, a gap of more than six years. A girl married before she finishes school often enters a household where she has little voice, few skills to earn, and no say in the decisions that shape her life. When such marriages break, she has the least to fall back on.
There is a darker side too. Lawyers and rights groups report men who make life unbearable so that their wives will file first, in the belief that this frees them from paying denmohor , the dower promised at marriage. Even women's "choice" to leave can be coerced.
For Rumana, filing was the easy part. The harder part begins after the 90 days. A divorced woman in Bangladesh still meets whispers at weddings, landlords who hesitate to rent to her, and relatives who ask what she did wrong. Remarriage is rare: BBS figures cited by officials show that only about 4% of widowed or divorced people remarry.
Men are not spared either, though their losses are less often discussed. Many lose regular contact with their children, and few seek help for the shame or loneliness that follows, in a culture that expects them to stay silent. Counselling services that could support both partners are almost absent outside a handful of private clinics in Dhaka.
Children carry much of the weight. The country has no institutional system to track what happens to families after divorce, so no one can say how many children are affected or how they fare. That silence matters in a country where, according to Unicef, nearly 90% of children aged 1-14 already face physical or emotional punishment at home each month; family breakdown can raise that risk further.
The law has not kept pace. Muslim divorce is still governed by the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance of 1961. Custody follows rules shaped by religious personal law, maintenance is hard to enforce, and many women never receive their dower. Hindu women, under their own personal law, have no clear right to divorce at all.
It is tempting to read the rising numbers as proof that the family is collapsing. A better reading is that more Bangladeshis, mostly women, are refusing marriages that were already broken. A society cannot wish divorce away, but it can decide how much it costs.
Three steps would help.
First, count properly : A national register that links divorce records to the children involved would let the state see who needs support.
Second, make the 90-day reconciliation period real : This has to be done with trained counsellors rather than a notice from a zonal office, and with fast-track enforcement of dower and child maintenance when reconciliation fails.
Third, reform personal laws: Every woman, whatever her religion, must have a clear and equal right to leave a marriage and to keep her children safe. Schools, employers and mosques can also help by treating divorced women and their children as neighbours, not cautionary tales.
Mahmodul Hasan Shesheir (Research Associate, Yale University, USA). Jinat Tamanna (MPH student, North South University) and Iftekhar Alam (undergraduate student, Chittagong Veterinary and Animal Sciences University).

US unveils proposed tariffs on major partners, including EU and China
item.description:
The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production -- the latest move by US President Donald Trump to remake Washington’s trade relationships.
The duties, proposed at up to 20%, come over allegations the economies “are promoting production and capacity divorced from the realities of demand and market principles,” a senior US official said on condition of anonymity.
The new tariffs will need to undergo a period of public comment before taking effect, with the official adding that the proposals take existing trade deals into account.
The new levies target some of the United States’ largest trading partners, including China, the European Union, India, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.
The US official made specific mention of China, for whom a 20% tariff is being proposed, the joint-highest for any economy.
In a separate announcement, the US Trade Representative’s office also proposed additional tariffs on goods from Brazil, including aircraft, over alleged inaction on addressing US trade concerns.
Trump’s tariffs have targeted Washington’s friends and foes alike, and are part of a push in his second term to remake global trade by forcing countries to buy US products or produce their goods in his country.
The latest move offers some relief for partners that earlier signed tariff deals with the Trump administration, but it could still raise temperatures as the US president prepares to host G20 leaders in Miami in December.
“We don’t expect this to create tension or rancor” at the G20 summit, the senior US official said. “We actually expect that we may be signing more agreements at the G20 in the wake of these announcements.”
Over-capacity concerns affect a range of sectors, from batteries to cement, chemicals to processed food, the senior US official said.
The duties could add further pressure on US businesses already squeezed by earlier tariffs, with firms now likelier to pass on costs to consumers already frustrated with the high cost of living.
Affordability was a key issue in recent midterm elections, which saw Trump’s Republican Party swept out of power in both houses of Congress by Democrats.
US consumer inflation came in at 3.7% year-on-year in September, close to a three-year high as prices are pushed up by the effects of Trump’s war on Iran, tariffs, and the massive AI investment boom.
US Federal Reserve policymakers, responsible for keeping inflation to a long-term two-percent target, say that most price effects of Trump’s previous tariff rollout have passed through the economy -- but any new levies could push prices up further.
The new tariffs are likely to come into effect in January at the earliest, the senior US official said.
Trump’s latest duties come after an investigation the US Trade Representative started in March on excess manufacturing capacity and production.
The concern was whether other countries were taking actions deemed “unreasonable or discriminatory,” and if they weighed on US commerce.
The probes came days after the US Supreme Court struck down Trump’s previous slew of tariffs, holding that the president did not hold the authority to impose the duties using the law the White House had cited.
Trade lawyer Ryan Majerus told AFP that he expected this probe to be among “the most important” actions for the Trump administration, given its underlying concern that factories with excess capacity start operations abroad and “never get turned off, even if there’s no demand.”
This potentially leads to an oversupply of goods, depressed prices and a “hollowing out” of US manufacturing, he added.
The US determination is likely to face strong pushback from China and others, with Beijing long rejecting criticism that it relies too much on exports to boost its economy.
While the US Supreme Court struck down Trump’s global tariffs in February, his sector-specific duties remain intact.
The new tariffs will not stack on top of those sector-specific tariffs on items like automobiles and steel, the senior US official said.
In July, Trump imposed a separate wave of tariffs on 60 economies, accusing them of insufficient action against forced labor.
For economies facing both the forced labor and excess production tariffs, the levies would not stack, the US official said. Instead, the higher rate of the two would prevail.

item.title: China space station receives Pakistani astronaut on ‘historic mission’
item.description:
China’s space station welcomed its first foreign lodger on Wednesday as a Pakistani astronaut boarded the Tiangong with his Shenzhou-24 mission crew, Beijing said.
China has poured billions into its space program as it aims to land astronauts on the Moon before 2030, a race in which the United States is also competing with its Artemis program.
The Shenzhou-24 crew’s Long March 2-F rocket took off in a cloud of flames and smoke Wednesday morning from the Jiuquan launch center in northwestern China under a pink sky, video from state broadcaster CCTV showed.
The spacecraft successfully separated from the carrier rocket roughly 10 minutes after blast-off and entered into orbit, the China Manned Space Agency (Cmsa) said.
The launch was a “complete success” and the crew was in good condition, the agency said.
After roughly three-and-a-half hours from launch, the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft successfully docked at the Tiangong space station, according to Cmsa.
Along with Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the latest mission is crewed by Chinese spacecraft pilot Tang Hongbo and Chinese flight engineer Wu Yi.
The three men “successfully moved into” the Tiangong, completing the first “space handshake” between Chinese and foreign astronauts, Cmsa said in a statement.
Pakistan and China are close diplomatic and strategic partners, and signed a deal in February 2025 setting up a Chinese government training program for Pakistani astronauts.
Chinese President Xi Jinping exchanged congratulations with his Pakistani counterpart after the launch, telling Asif Ali Zardari that Beijing stood ready to champion the “peaceful use of outer space” and “improve global space governance,” according to CCTV.
On Monday, Nato chief Mark Rutte said the alliance would defend against threats in space, after reports said Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite.
Now aboard the Tiangong station, Ali, a Pakistan Air Force pilot and payload specialist, is the first foreign astronaut to fly on a Chinese space mission.
Pakistan’s space agency said he would conduct experiments in orbit, including cultivating microalgae as a potential food and oxygen source for future space missions, and testing the effects of spaceflight on quinoa seeds.
The 40-year-old will join a short orbital flight expected to last around five days before returning with the Shenzhou-23 spaceship, which docked at the Tiangong space station in May.
That ship’s crew includes astronauts Zhu Yangzhu, Lai Ka-ying and Zhang Zhiyuan.
Lai is Hong Kong’s first astronaut and the only woman currently aboard.
Ali is not the first Pakistani in space, with Monaco-based polar adventurer Namira Salim having flown on Virgin Galactic’s Galactic 04 mission in October 2023.
Still, Pakistan’s Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Wednesday called the Shenzhou-24 launch a “historic mission,” marking a milestone in his country’s partnership with China.
“A proud moment for Pakistan, this mission will inspire our youth and advance our aspirations in science and technology,” he wrote on social media.
Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif previously hailed the mission as a testament to their close ties.
“Pakistan-China friendship is surpassing the heights of the Himalayas, in its journey to outer space,” he said.
Ali is scheduled to return to Earth alongside Lai and Zhang.
Zhu will remain on board to complete China’s first full-year stay in space -- a key test of endurance critical for future lunar and potentially deep-space ambitions.

item.title: UN warns of growing risk of atrocities by Israel against Palestinians
item.description:
The United Nations warned Wednesday of a growing risk of atrocity crimes being committed by Israel against the Palestinians, and urged all states to take immediate preventative action.
UN rights chief Volker Turk said ongoing Israeli attacks, policies and violations against Palestinians indicated a “widening risk of further atrocity crimes” in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip.
“Israeli government representatives at highest levels have time and again spelled out policies of annexation, ethnic cleansing and collective punishment in the West Bank,” he said in a statement.
“Across society, the incitement to hatred and to perpetration of violations amounting to atrocity crimes -- war crimes, crimes against humanity and even genocide -- has been appalling.”
Turk said his office had repeatedly warned about the risk of Israel’s actions in Gaza posing a “real threat to the continued existence” of the Palestinians as a group.
Most of Gaza’s population of 2.1 million live displaced in tents or makeshift shelters in the territory, where Israel’s military says it controls more than 60 percent of the land.
“I am extremely worried about the increasingly widespread and systematic nature of the violations being perpetrated across both the West Bank and Gaza,” Turk said.
“Our warnings have not been heeded, and atrocity crimes continue to recur,” said the UN high commissioner for human rights.
“Civilians continue to be killed, and hundreds of thousands of Palestinians have been forcibly displaced, with senior Israeli officials indicating intent for such displacement to be permanent.”
Violence in the West Bank, occupied by Israel since 1967, has surged since Hamas’s October 7, 2023 resistance campaign against Israel, which triggered the Gaza war.
“All states have the obligation to act, now, to prevent further atrocity crimes against the Palestinians,” said Turk.
“There must be independent investigations, and those responsible must be held to account. The work of the international courts in this regard must be supported by all states.”
Turk also reminded Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups of their obligations under international law, including to protect civilians and to respect the safety of humanitarian operations.

item.title: Scientists discover quasar formed 630 million years after the Big Bang
China warns US against imposing new tariffs
item.description:
Beijing urged the United States on Wednesday to “uphold the stable development” of trade relations, after media reports said Washington was planning to announce new tariffs on China and other countries.
The reports said that Washington’s new levies would affect major US trading partners including China, the European Union, Japan and South Korea.
“Tariff wars and trade wars are not in anyone’s interest,” Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said, when asked about Washington’s reported plans.
He told a regular briefing that the world’s two top economies, which in 2025 agreed a tenuous truce in their trade war, “should resolve relevant issues through consultation.”
He added that accusations of overcapacity -- mass production at a loss to flood overseas markets and undercut local rivals -- was a “false premise” and a “pretext for political manipulation.”
“China and the United States should work together to effectively implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state and uphold the stable development of China-US economic and trade relations,” he said.
President Donald Trump has long criticized China’s yawning trade surplus with the United States, which he has blamed for a decline in local manufacturing prowess and jobs.
After starting a second term in office last year, Trump imposed new tariffs on Chinese goods, kicking off a tit-for-tat escalation with Beijing that at one point saw duties soar as high as 145 percent.
The trade ceasefire struck by Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in October 2025 is due to expire in January, after a two-month extension was agreed in September.
The two men met last week at an Apec summit in Shenzhen in southern China and are due to see each other again in December at a G20 summit in the United States.
During their meeting at Apec, which came just before a historic trilateral with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Xi hailed China’s “stable and improved” ties with the United States.
The Chinese leader also said that his country should cooperate in the field of artificial intelligence, keeping the technology “under human control” and guarding against safety risks.

item.title: Saudi coalition says struck Yemen port city, Houthis threaten retaliation
item.description:
The Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis said Wednesday it had struck Yemen’s key port city of Hodeida, while the Iran-backed group threatened to retaliate as the conflict further escalated.
The Houthis also claimed responsibility for attacks a day earlier on the Saudi capital that struck the tallest tower in its financial district, wounding 11.
In recent weeks the group has launched a barrage at Saudi targets including the financial district, airports, energy infrastructure and military sites.
The Saudi coalition has been striking Houthi-held areas of Yemen in support of the internationally recognized government, which has been battling the Houthis for territory since a civil war reignited in July.
“We targeted operational capabilities at the port of Hodeida,” the coalition posted to X on Wednesday, having earlier warned civilians to evacuate.
Hodeidah is under Houthi control and is a key entry point for goods into Yemeni territory held by the group.
Houthi media outlet Almasirah confirmed Hodeida had been targeted but did not provide details. No casualties or injuries were reported.
Almasirah added that Saudi forces had also attacked the area’s international airport.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree early on Wednesday threatened to retaliate against Red Sea ports in Saudi Arabia if the coalition went ahead with strikes on Hodeida.
“The port of Jeddah, along with all other Saudi enemy ports along the Red Sea coast, will become targets for our forces should the enemy carry out its threats,” he posted on Telegram.
Saree warned civilians near Saudi ports to “evacuate immediately” and called for “all shipping companies to remove their vessels from these ports at once.”
Months into the renewed war, Saudi Arabia appears increasingly unable to shield even its most sensitive infrastructure from attacks, with the Houthis striking strategic facilities across the kingdom and prominent skyscrapers in the heart of Riyadh.
On the ground in Yemen, the Houthis are pressing their advance against government forces, forcing them to retreat. Houthi fighters are positioned just 60 kilometers (37 miles) from Aden, the government’s main stronghold in the south.
A Yemeni military spokesman said this week that they were preparing Aden’s defenses for a potential attack.
In a sign of mounting pressure on Riyadh, Saudi Arabia last week removed its top general overseeing its military campaign, in what appeared to be an effort to inject new momentum into the war and contain their adversaries.
On Tuesday, the Saudi capital’s tallest skyscraper was struck for a second time in days, wounding 11 people.
The Houthis claimed responsibility on Wednesday, also saying they struck the sprawling Ras Tanura refinery in the kingdom’s oil-rich east.
Saree described the refinery attack as “accurate and direct”, saying it “caused fires to break out at the facility.”
Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki said early Wednesday they had intercepted and destroyed four drones in Ras Tanura, resulting in falling shrapnel but no reported injuries.
Saree said the Houthi attack on Riyadh was carried out in three phases, with strikes also hitting their targets “accurately.”
The Riyadh attack struck the PIF tower, which houses the Saudi sovereign wealth fund. The building had already been targeted last Thursday and is one of several high-profile sites hit since fighting resumed in the summer.
Attacks on the PIF are symbolic as the fund is driving efforts to diversify the oil-reliant Saudi economy -- a project that has been complicated by the Middle East war and Houthi strikes.
Qatar and Pakistan, who have been acting as mediators in efforts to end the wider regional war between Iran and the United States, both “strongly” condemned the attack on the building.
Two Indian citizens were wounded in the attack, Delhi’s foreign ministry said.

item.title: Jubo Dal leader feeds AL leader eggs, coffee before handing him over to police
item.description:
Rabiul Islam Nayan, member secretary of the Dhaka Metropolitan South Jubo Dal, detained an Awami League leader in the capital's Paltan area on Tuesday night and handed him over to police after treating him to boiled eggs, water and coffee.
The detained man was identified as Javed Didar, who introduced himself as the general secretary of Ward 26 of the Dhaka Metropolitan South Awami League's Lalbagh unit.
Nayan and his associates detained Javed at around 10pm. Nayan later shared a video of the incident on his verified Facebook account, identifying the time and location.
In the video, Nayan is seen questioning Javed about his identity and why he was in the area. After Javed identified himself as an Awami League leader, Nayan remarked that he would offer him some eggs.
An associate then handed Nayan a boiled egg. Although Javed initially refused, Nayan urged him to eat one, saying he would eat one too. Javed eventually ate the egg, followed by Nayan. The video shows Javed being given two boiled eggs in total.
Nayan then asked an associate to bring a bottle of water.
While escorting Javed on foot, Nayan alleged that the Awami League leader had been planning sabotage in the Gulistan area ahead of Sheikh Hasina's expected arrival.
He said he had detained him and given him two eggs and water to keep him strong, adding that he was taking him along with respect.
The activists accompanying Nayan chanted slogans calling for Awami League members to be arrested and jailed.
In the video, Nayan also warned that anyone in Dhaka Metropolitan South involved in alleged sabotage would not be spared. His associates later chanted slogans urging people to arrest Awami League members rather than focus on December.
The video also shows Nayan taking Javed to a coffee shop, where he offered him coffee and fed him by hand.
During the conversation, Nayan recalled how BNP and Jubo Dal activists were treated after being arrested during the previous Awami League government. He said he himself had spent 77 consecutive days on remand during that period.
Towards the end of the video, Nayan told Javed not to be afraid. When police arrived, Nayan handed over Javed's mobile phone. Police then took the Awami League leader out of the coffee shop and into a vehicle.
Paltan police station Officer-in-Charge Ariful Alam told the media that Javed, who had identified himself as an Awami League leader, was taken to the police station following the detention.
He said legal action would be taken after verifying the details.

item.title: ULAB faculty member completes residency at translation workshop
item.description:
University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh (ULAB) faculty member Arifa Ghani Rahman, head of the Department of English and Humanities, participated in a 3-day residential translation workshop held from November 16–18, 2026.
The workshop was jointly organized by South Asian Literatures in Translation (SALT) and BRAC University’s Department of English and Humanities.
A recipient of the SALT-English PEN 2026 Translation Grant, Rahman was selected through a blind review of her sample translation. She was among 26 participants selected from 53 applicants across Bangladesh.
The workshop featured translation experts Jason Grunebaum of the University of Chicago, Daniel Hahn, OBE, and Bangladeshi translator Shabnam Nadiya as facilitators.
Grunebaum and Hahn are the proponents of SALT.
The residency included plenary sessions, discussions with language experts and collaborative translation workshops, offering participants opportunities to refine their skills and explore the art and science of literary translation.

Actor Mamunur Rashid admitted to ICU with pneumonia
item.description:
Veteran actor and theatre personality Mamunur Rashid has been admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) of Labaid Hospital in Dhaka after falling seriously ill with pneumonia.
He has been receiving treatment at the hospital for the past three days, the Actors’ Equity Bangladesh confirmed.
The organisation’s General Secretary Rashed Mamun Opu said Rashid was admitted after being diagnosed with pneumonia. The actor had also required ICU treatment during a previous bout of serious illness.
On April 30, 2025, Rashid fell ill aboard a flight to the United States. Medical tests there revealed pneumonia in both lungs and a bloodstream infection. He spent six days in the ICU before recovering and returning home. After staying in the United States for an extended period, he returned to Bangladesh on January 14.
Rashid has worked in theatre, television and films for more than five decades. Besides acting, he is widely recognised as a playwright and director. He founded the prominent theatre troupe Aranyak in 1972.
